{{further|2026 National Bank Open}}

[[Iga Świątek]] defeated [[Elena Rybakina]] in the final, 6–2, 6–3 to win the women's singles tennis title at the [[2026 National Bank Open|2026 Canadian Open]]. It was her twelfth [[WTA 1000]] title and her 26th [[WTA Tour]] title overall.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4559201/swiatek-ends-yearlong-title-drought-in-toronto-after-sweeping-past-rybakina-in-straight-sets|title=Swiatek wins first title of 2026 in Toronto after sweeping past Rybakina|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|date=13 August 2026}}</ref> 

[[Victoria Mboko]] was the reigning champion,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4336282/mboko-completes-dream-week-with-win-over-osaka-in-montreal|title=Mboko completes dream week with win over Osaka in Montreal|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|date=8 August 2025}}</ref> but did not participate due to a knee injury.<ref>{{Citeweb|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4532192/defending-champion-victoria-mboko-to-miss-national-bank-open-in-toronto|title=Defending champion Mboko to miss National Bank Open in Toronto|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=7 July 2026}}</ref>

[[Aryna Sabalenka]] retained the [[List of WTA number 1 ranked singles tennis players|WTA No. 1 singles ranking]] by reaching the fourth round. Rybakina was also in contention at the beginning of the tournament.<ref>{{Citeweb|url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/4551695/whats-at-stake-how-rybakina-can-overtake-sabalenka-for-no-1-in-toronto|title=What's at stake: How Rybakina can overtake Sabalenka for No. 1 in Toronto|publisher=Women's Tennis Association|accessdate=1 August 2026}}</ref>
